faqs.question: What is the difference between a water bath and a circulating bath?
faqs.answer: A water bath holds a static temperature with no fluid movement, while a circulating bath actively pumps fluid, both internally and to external processes; choose a water bath when your application doesn't require circulation.

faqs.question: What is the temperature range of the Digital General Purpose Water Bath?
faqs.answer: Ambient+5°C to 100°C, with uniformity to ±0.2°C and stability to ±0.1°C.

faqs.question: Can this water bath run without water?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's also compatible with waterless bath beads, so a liquid fill isn't required.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right reservoir capacity?
faqs.answer: Match the capacity to your typical sample volume: 2 or 5 liters for compact bench work, or 20 to 28 liters for larger batches; Inkarp confirms the exact fit for your application.

faqs.question: How do I set up a repeatable temperature and timer combination?
faqs.answer: Program the temperature and duration as a preset once, and recall it at the press of a button for every subsequent run, without re-entering the values.

faqs.question: Do all sizes include a reservoir drain?
faqs.answer: No. Only the 10-liter and larger models include a drain; the 2 and 5-liter baths do not.

faqs.question: What material is the reservoir made from?
faqs.answer: 304 stainless steel, across every capacity in the line.

faqs.question: What languages does the interface support?
faqs.answer: Five selectable languages, in a plain-language menu system.

faqs.question: What safety features are built in?
faqs.answer: Primary and automatic safety thermostats, a user-settable high limit value, and audible or visible alarms.

faqs.question: What is Eco Mode?
faqs.answer: An automatic power-saving mode that activates once a timed run completes.

body: The controls on this line are built around one idea: set it up once, and never re-enter the same values again.

Presets store the temperature and duration combinations you use regularly, recalled with one press rather than re-dialed every time. Eco Mode takes over automatically once a timed run finishes, and the integrated timer plus user-settable alarms mean a run doesn't need to be watched to be trusted.

faqs.question: What is the Viscosity Water Bath used for?
faqs.answer: It's a temperature-controlled bath purpose-built for capillary viscometer testing under ASTM D-445, commonly used for petroleum, lubricant, and chemical viscosity measurement.

faqs.question: Why does this bath use a glass reservoir?
faqs.answer: Capillary viscosity testing requires visually timing fluid movement through the viscometer, which a glass reservoir allows and a stainless steel one would block entirely.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the AD and MX controllers?
faqs.answer: Match the controller to your precision needs and testing volume: confirm with Inkarp whether AD offers tighter stability for your application, since this line doesn't state per-controller precision separately.

faqs.question: How do I set up the included cooling coil?
faqs.answer: Connect the coil to a tap water supply; it provides supplemental cooling support without requiring a separate chiller unit.

faqs.question: What viscometers does this bath support?
faqs.answer: It's configured for popular capillary viscometer types, with Inkarp confirming exact fit against your specific model.

faqs.question: What temperature range does this bath cover?
faqs.answer: Up to 200°C, with stability to ±0.01°C.

faqs.question: Does this bath come in different capacities?
faqs.answer: No. This line is offered at a fixed 17-liter capacity; the controller type is the primary configuration choice.

faqs.question: What is the difference between this and the Digital General Purpose Water Bath?
faqs.answer: The Viscosity Bath is purpose-built for ASTM D-445 testing with a glass reservoir and higher temperature range, while the General Purpose line covers everyday laboratory heating with a stainless steel reservoir up to 100°C.

faqs.question: What is DuraTop?
faqs.answer: An insulating, chemical-resistant deck material used across PolyScience's bath lines, including this one.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Viscosity Water Bath (17 L) in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the controller type you choose. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your testing requirements are confirmed.

sections.title: Viscometer Compatibility and Visual Monitoring
sections.tabSummary: Why glass, and what it fits
body: A viscosity test is only as good as your ability to see it happen, and that's the entire reason this bath is built the way it is.

Capillary viscometers rely on visually timing fluid as it moves through a narrow tube, which a stainless steel reservoir would hide completely. The glass reservoir keeps that visible throughout, while the lidded openings hold the viscometer in the correct position without leaving the bath uncovered. Configured for popular capillary viscometer types, the bath is built to slot directly into an existing ASTM D-445 testing workflow.
